messages.author: b2b2b752fe3de41b
messages.subject: modeling left-truncated and right-censored data
parts:
Hi,

    I am able to build working examples for either left-truncated or right-censored data. However I am not able to figure out how to specify both. 
    Does anyone know how to specify Stan code for right-censored data from a left-truncated distribution?
    ### simulated data
    dplyr
    set.seed(12345)
    dat2 <- data.frame(x1 = runif(n, -2, 2),
                                   x2 = runif(n, -1, 1), 
                                     y = unlist(lapply(mu + x1 * b1 + x2 * b2, rlnorm, n = 1, sdlog = 1.5)),                       
                                  lmt = sample(seq(300, 500, 100), n, replace = TRUE)) %>%                     ### censoring at 300 to 500
                                  mutate(yc           = pmin(y, y1),                                                                    ### censored response
                                             censored = ifelse(y > y1, 1, 0)) %>%
                                  filter(yc > 50)                                                                                               ### truncated @ 50 

    I am trying to model yc with x1 and x2 using lognormal family. 

Thanks,
Allen

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modeling left-truncated and right-censored data
parts:
The truncation below at 0 is built into the lognormal, so you
only need the upper bound, so it'll work just like a right-censored
variable.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modeling left-truncated and right-censored data
parts:
Yes, the truncation logic doesn't change just because the
underlying density/mass function is itself truncated.

You can convince yourself of that by fitting a simple
truncated distribution to simple truncated data.

- Bob
